title: introduce-policy-driven-cost-profiles-and-quant-candidate-ranker
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add policy-driven default profiles for batching/caching and a quantization candidate ranking service; new CLI subcommand `rw econ profile` and Console UI hooks. Non-breaking; opt-in via config flag.
description:
Motivation:
We need an automated way to propose safe, route-scoped defaults for batching, KV-caching and quantization that balances unit economics with latency SLAs. Current on-call and SRE workflows rely on hand-tuned presets per-customer which doesn't scale. This PR implements a policy-driven defaults engine plus a lightweight quantization candidate ranker to surface safe quant profiles to operators and an opt-in CLI to apply curated profiles at scale.

Summary of changes (high level):
- New service: optimizer/policyprofiles — evaluates route metadata (model, seq distribution, priority tier) against policy rules and outputs default profiles for batching, cache TTL/size, and quantization candidates.
- New service: optimizer/quantranker — scores candidate quantization configurations using a multi-metric heuristic (inference latency delta, throughput delta, per-token cost delta, and a model-quality regression proxy).
- CLI: cmd/rw-econ profile apply/list/preview — preview ranked profiles and apply them to a route or model variant.
- Console hooks: small REST endpoints and UI feature flags to show previewed profile recommendations (UI PRs will follow).
- Integration tests and e2e harness for sampling real trace histograms to validate no-regression rules.

Why different from existing autotuners:
- Policy-first: operators write expressive policies (latency SLO bounds, cost targets, aversion to quality drop) instead of tuning knobs. The engine composes policies with workload signals to produce conservative defaults and an ordered set of quant candidates for experimentation.
- Ranking over discrete quant candidates rather than blindly recommending a single quant profile. The ranker exposes trade-offs so teams can select by cost or latency budgets.
- CLI + API + telemetry: full UX path for preview -> apply -> observe.

Design notes and implementation details:
- Profiles are generated per-route and per-model-variant. A profile includes: target_batch_size, max_latency_p99_ms, prefill_policy (none/light/heavy), kv_cache_ttl_seconds, kv_cache_max_entries, quant_candidate_ids (ordered).
- Quant candidates are generated by enumerating supported quant flavors (int8, q4_0, q4_1, q5_0, quant-mlir candidates) combined with per-layer hints; a fast estimator runs microbenchmarks on representative token lengths to estimate throughput/latency impact.
- The ranker score = w1 * normalized_cost_reduction + w2 * normalized_latency_impact + w3 * regression_risk_score. We set conservative defaults (w3 high) for previews; teams can tune weights in policy.
- Safety gates: any candidate that predicts >2% quality regression (via lightweight ngram/embedding drift proxy) is demoted and requires a manual opt-in. The preview always includes a 'safe' baseline candidate (no quant).
- Persistence: profiles are stored in config store under /optimizer/profiles/{team}/{route}. Applying a profile triggers a rollout job (canary by default) and emits events to telemetry.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for policy parsing, candidate scoring, and CLI output.
- Integration job (optimizer-integration) runs microbench harness in CI container with a mocked GPU runtime to validate latency estimates (ci matrix includes small and large runs).
- CI initially failed due to a race in rollout controller tests (see review comments); fixed by moving to deterministic backoff and adding a test hook. Final CI status: all jobs passed.

Review conversation (selected snippets):
- Diego Ramos (review): "Nice separation between policy language and scoring. Two asks: (1) make the quant candidate enumeration deterministic for reproducible previews; (2) we need clearer telemetry for before/after token-level cost delta per-route."
- Author (Maya): "Agreed on deterministic enumeration — changed the generator to sort by model seed+config and added explicit stable IDs. Added a telemetry event that emits per-route token-cost estimate and observed post-rollout token-cost."
- Li Wei (review): "Can we tighten the regression proxy? Ngram drift is noisy for small corpora. Suggest adding an embedding-distance-based check as a second signal."
- Author (Maya): "Added embedding-drift check (cosine threshold) and exposed an override in policy to prefer either signal. Kept default conservative (both signals must fire to demote candidate)."
- Hannah Schmidt (approve): "Approach and safety gates look good. Recommend we ship behind feature flag and add a migration note for customers that expect static presets."

Checklist:
- [x] Policy language + parser implemented
- [x] Quant candidate ranker + microbench harness
- [x] CLI preview/apply/list implemented
- [x] Integration tests + CI job added
- [x] Telemetry events and dashboards skeleton (console UI TBD)
- [x] Feature gated (env var: OPTIMIZER_POLICY_PROFILES=true)

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main behind feature flag.
- Enable feature flag for internal beta tenants and run an A/B canary on low-traffic routes for 2 weeks.
- Collect telemetry: token-level cost delta, latency P50/P95/P99, error/regression proxies.
- Iterate weight defaults based on observed trade-offs, then widen to more tenants.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- No breaking changes to API. Config store introduces new keys but falls back to previous behavior when absent.

Notes for ops:
- New CI job 'optimizer-integration' may add ~10 minutes to matrix runtime; maintainers can opt out for quick patches.
- To preview recommendations for a route: `rw-econ profile preview --route /v1/generate --model redwood/galactica-7b`

Merge outcome:
- After iterative fixes (deterministic enumeration and embedding-drift signal) the PR was approved by QA and SRE. Squash-merged into main. Merge commit includes scoped changelog entry and release note.

Follow-ups (tracked):
- Console UI: show ranked quant candidates and preview diff (UI-PL-78).
- Eval harness integration: verify quality with full eval suites for promoted quant candidates (ENG-3459).
- Opt-in autopilot that runs short experiments for top candidate and can auto-promote on success (future work).
